instructions: Answer the questions below. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You will hear a conversation between a professor and a student about a play direction project.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: First, you have some time to read through questions 8 to 11.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Now, listen carefully and answer questions 8 to 11.

transcript.speaker: Professor
transcript.text: So you've been working on your one-act play project assigned for your directing course. Tell me what you've done so far, Sarah.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Well, at first I thought about directing a kind of Alaska by Harold Pinter. It has a small cast and wouldn't be too complicated to direct, so that would have been another advantage. But it is a very serious drama.

transcript.speaker: Professor
transcript.text: Why would that be a problem?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: There are a lot of other students in our course doing serious dramas, and I wanted to do something which would stand out a bit. So I decided to do a comedy.
transcript.highlight_text: So I decided to do a comedy.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: I read through several scripts of contemporary one-act works, but, uh, I didn't find anything that really appealed to me.

transcript.speaker: Professor
transcript.text: Did you read any scripts that were older? You know, classic plays?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: I did, and that's when I found a script called Dark Lady of the Sonnets by George Bernard Shaw.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: It was written about 100 years ago, but the story is about William Shakespeare in Elizabethan England in the late 1500s, so it is said about 500 years ago.
transcript.highlight_text: It was written about 100 years ago

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Anyway, I chose it in the end because it has a very classical feel, yet is still quite contemporary.

transcript.speaker: Professor
transcript.text: Hmm, that sounds great, Sarah. I know the play well. Although it was written in the early 1900s, it does have a very contemporary point of view with regard to feminism. I think that would be very interesting, and it presents some exciting challenges in terms of direction.

transcript.speaker: Professor
transcript.text: So, now, I guess you need to think about casting and set. Have you thought about those things yet?

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: Ah, a bit. The original script calls for a complicated set, but it would take too much time to build something like that. I think I will do a very simple set.
transcript.highlight_text: I think I will do a very simple set.

transcript.speaker: Professor
transcript.text: Yes, that's true, Sarah, but fortunately the university has an old set from Romeo and Juliet in storage. It includes a balcony, which is a necessary component of the play you will be directing.
transcript.highlight_text: It includes a balcony, which is a necessary component

transcript.speaker: Professor
transcript.text: It also features a fireplace, which would be interesting to use. All you have to do is set it all up.

transcript.speaker: Sarah
transcript.text: That may be true, but it is quite a large set. It would take a lot of time to assemble.

transcript.speaker: Professor
transcript.text: Okay, I understand. So, Sarah, what types of actors will you need for the play?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: You now have 15 seconds to check your answers.

questions.question_text: What type of play has Sarah chosen to direct?
questions.explanation: Sarah decides to do something that stands out from the serious dramas others are doing, choosing a 'comedy'.

questions.question_text: How many years ago was Dark Lady of the Sonnets written?
questions.explanation: Sarah mentions the script 'was written about 100 years ago'.

questions.question_text: How does Sarah describe the set she is going to build?
questions.explanation: Sarah states she will do a 'very simple set' because a complicated one would take too much time.

questions.question_text: Which element of the old set is essential for Sarah?
questions.explanation: The professor mentions the old set includes a 'balcony', which is a 'necessary component' for the play.
